## TL;DR

This round answers the review verdict "needs some work" on the markdown list-marker guard, and it reruns the headless QA pass on this tree. The guard now covers computed-property surfaces (`v-html="specHtml"`), not only literal `renderMarkdown(...)` calls. The guard's static blind spot was the reason `.md-rendered` and `release-update-markdown` lost enforcement. I also fixed a harness false positive that failed the "dialog fits" check about half the time, and I corrected the overstated comment and QA doc. The scoped `repoos check` is green. One harness timeout is still unexplained: it failed once in eleven post-fix runs and did not reproduce in six more. I have not claimed it as fixed.

## Work and rationale

The review's blocking item was that `markdown-list-markers.test.ts` matched only `v-html="render(Chat)?Markdown(...)"` written literally in the template. That missed `.md-rendered` (StoryPanel, TaskDrawer, ContextView, InputsView) and `.release-update-markdown` (ReleaseUpdateNotification), whose HTML comes from computed properties. Removing `.md-rendered ul` from the shared rule therefore failed no test. The comment in `style.css` and the QA doc both claimed the scan covered every site, which was false.

I checked the whole class instead of patching the two named surfaces. Every `v-html` in `src/ui-app/src` is in one of two groups. Files that import `renderMarkdown` or `renderChatMarkdown` render markdown through every `v-html` they contain. Files that don't import them (SearchOverlay, MobileTabs, FeedPanel, Sidebar, DiffView, SettingsView) have no markdown `v-html`. So the test now treats any `v-html` in a file that imports the renderer as a markdown surface. That covers both literal calls and computed names, and it needs no per-name allowlist. I kept the scan keyed by an array, not a map, because the old map overwrote entries for two sites with the same file and tag. Names now carry the line number, so a failure points at one `<div>` rather than several identical rows.

I also restored the static enforcement the review asked for. `REQUIRED_CONTAINERS` lists the eight classes the shared rule must cover, and each one must still have disc and decimal rules. The mutation check removed `.md-rendered ul`/`ol` from `style.css` and nine checks failed, then I restored the file from git.

For the docs, I rewrote the `style.css` comment and QA §4 to say exactly what the scan covers. The known limit is that markdown rendered by a child component is not scanned, so its container class must be added by hand. I fixed the "The The" typo, corrected the vitest count to 89, and rewrote the verification paragraph with the real run data.

The QA harness had its own problems, which I fixed in the script and recorded in the doc. Its "dialog fits" check failed on "Read more on GitHub" in about half of the runs. The cause is a harness false positive. The link wraps onto two lines, `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the union box of its fragments, and the centre of that box falls in the gap between lines, so `elementFromPoint` returns the paragraph. `covered()` now hit-tests each `getClientRects()` fragment. The fit checks also print their measurements on failure, which they did not before, so a real overflow would show its numbers. `shot()` now waits 400 ms for the dialog's entrance fade, because the first capture showed the modal half-transparent.

## Approaches tried

I first considered widening the regex to match computed names by name. That fails because the names (`specHtml`, `reviewHtml`, `notesHtml`) carry no marker. Matching on the file's renderer import is simpler and exact for this codebase, and I checked that claim against the full `v-html` list before relying on it.

For the fit check, I first assumed the dialog's entrance animation caused the failures. The `running` animation list supported that, but the decisive evidence was `rects: 2` and a 32 px box for a single link. The fragment fix was the one that removed the failure in every later run.

## Challenges and blockers

The first harness run after the guard change showed three failures. Over the next runs the fit failures moved between widths and checks, which looked like a flake. Printing the measurements turned it into a deterministic geometry issue that only varied with subpixel position, so I did not treat it as flaky after that.

One intermittent failure remains open. After the fix, one of eleven runs failed `supervised: scenario ran @375`, a 5 s timeout waiting for the "Restart is waiting" line after Restart when idle. Six further runs were clean. The UI refreshes status 1.5 s after the POST, and the harness waits 5 s, so the margin looks adequate. I suspect either a real race or harness load, but I have not confirmed either. I did not lengthen the wait, because that would hide a possible product race. The QA doc records it as open.

Handoff hit a git lock earlier: `index.lock` in the main checkout's worktree metadata. When I looked, a `claude -p` session for another task was running. I did not confirm that it held the lock, so I did not remove the lock file, and I did not touch the main checkout. Handoff should be retried once no other git process holds it. The self-check committed my four changed files as a WIP checkpoint (`1d49b7c52`), so nothing is left uncommitted in this worktree.

## Key learnings

A regex scan of a template is only as complete as its match pattern. The file-level rule (imports the renderer, so every `v-html` is markdown) is more robust than matching names. Measuring with a `getBoundingClientRect()` union box is not a hit-test for wrapped inline elements. Test each fragment.

The shot and fit checks need their own settle and failure detail, or a single flaky assertion looks like a product bug. Printing the measurements decided the question quickly.

## Human follow-up

- No real server was restarted. Restart and dismiss were verified against fixtures only. A human should run one real hand-run restart on a disposable server before anyone claims the restart path works.
- The top-bar "New version available" button calls `repo.restartServer()` directly, with no dialog, no "Restart when idle" and no dismiss. It was outside this pass's four states and is a candidate for a follow-up task.
- The sidebar version label is hidden at 375 and 768 px. The version still appears in the restart notice and the release modal, so no information is lost, but I did not trace the CSS cause.
- The open intermittent timeout above needs a longer soak run or a cause.
- The three declared review shots are fixture states on the preview board, so RepoOS captures them at handoff. I checked the harness captures of the release modal (bullets visible) and the failure notice (command named) at 375 px on this tree.
